text:
maria: Heads-up — exploring adding a client-side "policy-gates" layer into SDKs to catch or transform requests before they hit the API for certain sensitive customers. Want to discuss tradeoffs (compat, telemetry, rollout UX).

ashok: server-side should remain source of truth. client gates improve UX (no back-and-forth) but create more SDK surface area to maintain. risk of inconsistent enforcement across old clients. :thinking_face:

jon: can we make it opt-in? e.g. env / constructor flag `enablePolicyGates=true` so we can roll gradually.

maria: yeah. also need `mode` flag: `warn|dry-run|enforce|auto-correct`. dry-run sends telemetry but doesn't block. example idea: SDK downloads a small policy schema from control plane and validates locally.

linda: breaking-change risk: if a new policy blocks old clients they might error out. suggest default to `warn` and 1) log telemetry 2) surface console warnings 3) provide clear upgrade guide.

paul: parity across py/ts/go will be annoying. prefer a single JSON schema served by control plane + language runtimes implement a thin validator. maybe ship TS first then port. use shared schema and semantic versioning.

samir: telemetry note: emit `policy.decision` events with `decision=allowed|blocked|modified`, `policy_id`, `reason_code`. sample rate and PII redaction. also surface a console tile showing clients in `warn` vs `enforce`.

maria: quick config sketch (pseudo):
```json
{
  "policy_mode": "dry-run",
  "allowed_models": ["redwood-base-1","rwd-small"],
  "max_tokens": 2048,
  "regions": ["us-west-2"]
}
```
SDK would validate request fields against this, and either attach a `X-Redwood-Policy-Decision` header or throw depending on mode.

jon: tests: unit + e2e with a local policy-engine stub. need integration test that ensures server & client decisions align when enforce=true.

ci-bot: deploy scheduled: canary branch `policy-gates/ts` -> dev-org on 2026-04-15T09:00Z.

linda: UX: errors should be actionable: e.g. `request blocked: model not allowed for org. try rwd-small or contact infra-team`. include `retryable: false` flag. include safe fallback header `X-Redwood-Policy-Action: blocked|modified|allowed`.

ashok: consider server returning `suggested_model` in rejection payload so SDK can auto-retry if in `auto-correct` mode. avoids two-step manual mapping.

paul: perf: local validation should be extremely cheap (schema + a few checks). need to measure impact on cold start for Go + Py. also think about caching schema and invalidation (etag).

maria: rollout plan proposal:
1) eng-platform: expose policy schema endpoint + versioning (ashok)
2) SDKs: implement dry-run + telemetry + `policy_mode` config (jon/paul)
3) devex: docs + migration guide + console mockups (linda)
4) runtime: perf tests + fallback behaviors (paul)
5) telemetry: spec events + console visualization (samir)

maria: ask: who can own the initial TS + Py dry-run prototype?

jon: I can take TS prototype, will start a small RFC in repo.

paul: I’ll do Py and coordinate on schema.

linda: devex will draft upgrade guide and sample error messages.

samir: I’ll write the telemetry schema and a console sketch for the tile.

ashok: I’ll draft the control-plane schema endpoints & auth model.

jon: +1

paul: slicing tasks now.

maria: thanks everyone. syncing tomorrow 10:00am PT to lock the spec. :calendar: :pray:

jon: small Q — do we want SDKs to auto-update schema? auto-pull with backoff or require explicit `refresh()`? both have pros/cons.

linda: prefer auto-pull with long TTL and opt-out. document how to disable.

maria: noted — add to decision log.

paul: will add a flag `policySchemaAutoRefresh=true|false` and `refreshInterval=3600s`.

maria: copilot: moving to action items in the RFC. thanks all.

jon: thanks!
